# Types

Each field's Postgres type comes from its proto type and `format`, unless
`(dal.pg.v1.column)` overrides it. The Go type comes from the proto type and
the column's nullability. Generated code never uses pgx's `pgtype` wrappers:
every type below is a plain Go type.

## The default mapping

<!-- generated:type-defaults:begin -->
<!-- Code generated by internal/docgen. DO NOT EDIT; run `mise run docs`. -->

| Proto (+ `format`) | Postgres | Go | Go when `optional` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `string`, an enum | `text` | `string` | `*string` |
| `string` + `FORMAT_UUID` | `uuid` | `uuid.UUID` | `*uuid.UUID` |
| `string` + `FORMAT_DECIMAL` | `numeric` | `string` | `*string` |
| `string` + `FORMAT_JSON`, a message, `google.protobuf.Struct`, `google.protobuf.Value`, `google.protobuf.ListValue` | `jsonb` | `json.RawMessage` | `json.RawMessage` |
| `bool` | `boolean` | `bool` | `*bool` |
| `int32`, `sint32`, `sfixed32` | `integer` | `int32` | `*int32` |
| `int64`, `sint64`, `sfixed64`, `uint32`, `fixed32` | `bigint` | `int64` | `*int64` |
| `uint64`, `fixed64` | none: needs a `custom_type` ([DAL209](lint-rules.md#dal209)) |  |  |
| `float` | `real` | `float32` | `*float32` |
| `double` | `double precision` | `float64` | `*float64` |
| `bytes` | `bytea` | `[]byte` | `[]byte` |
| `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | `timestamptz` | `time.Time` | `*time.Time` |
| `repeated string` | `text[]` | `[]string` | (can't be `optional`) |
| `repeated int64` | `bigint[]` | `[]int64` | (can't be `optional`) |
| `repeated google.protobuf.Timestamp` | `timestamptz[]` | `[]time.Time` | (can't be `optional`) |
| `repeated` message, `map<…>` | `jsonb` | `json.RawMessage` | (can't be `optional`) |
<!-- generated:type-defaults:end -->

Other well-known types (`Duration`, wrappers such as `StringValue`, `Any`)
aren't supported. Use the plain type with `optional` instead of a wrapper.

### Notes

- **Timestamps** are stored as `timestamptz`, with microsecond precision, so
  Postgres rounds Go's nanoseconds. Compare times read back from the database
  with `Equal`, not `==`.
- **Decimals** are `string` in Go. That's exact in both directions: a 30-digit
  value round-trips unchanged. To use a decimal library instead, see
  [Custom types](#custom-types). **For money, prefer `int64` minor units**
  (cents), as the example does: they're exact, fast and easy to sum.
- **Enums** are stored as `text`, and the generated Go type is `string`, so
  your code decides the values. Store the value name (`"COLOR_RED"`): it's
  readable in SQL and survives renumbering. The schema has no `CHECK`
  constraint, because adding a value would then need a migration before the
  code could use it. The generated code doesn't validate enum values yet.
- **JSON** (`FORMAT_JSON`, messages, maps) is stored as `jsonb` and handed to
  you as raw bytes. Marshal and unmarshal with whatever you like.

## Overriding the Postgres type

`(dal.pg.v1.column).type` picks another first-class type. The Go type stays
the one the proto type implies, so only compatible types are allowed
([DAL209](lint-rules.md#dal209)):

<!-- generated:type-overrides:begin -->
<!-- Code generated by internal/docgen. DO NOT EDIT; run `mise run docs`. -->

| Proto | Allowed `type` values |
|---|---|
| `string` | `TYPE_TEXT`, `TYPE_UUID`, `TYPE_NUMERIC`, `TYPE_JSONB`, `TYPE_INET` |
| `int32` | `TYPE_SMALLINT`, `TYPE_INTEGER`, `TYPE_BIGINT` |
| `int64` | `TYPE_BIGINT` |
| `uint32` | `TYPE_BIGINT` |
| `float` | `TYPE_REAL`, `TYPE_DOUBLE_PRECISION` |
| `double` | `TYPE_DOUBLE_PRECISION` |
| `bool` | `TYPE_BOOLEAN` |
| `bytes` | `TYPE_BYTEA` |
| `Timestamp` | `TYPE_TIMESTAMPTZ`, `TYPE_DATE` |
| an enum | `TYPE_TEXT` |
<!-- generated:type-overrides:end -->

```proto
  google.protobuf.Timestamp day = 1 [(dal.pg.v1.column).type = TYPE_DATE];
  string client_ip = 2 [(dal.pg.v1.column).type = TYPE_INET];   // Go: string
```

Prefer `format` where one exists: `FORMAT_UUID` also changes the Go type,
whereas `type: TYPE_UUID` on a plain `string` keeps Go `string`.

## Custom types

For anything outside the table, such as extension types, parameterised types
or your own Go type, use `custom_type` with `go_type`:

```proto
option (dal.pg.v1.file) = {extensions: ["vector"]};

message Document {
  …
  string embedding = 5 [(dal.pg.v1.column) = {   // the proto type only documents intent here
    custom_type: "vector(1536)"
    go_type: "github.com/pgvector/pgvector-go.Vector"
  }];
  string price = 6 [(dal.pg.v1.column) = {
    custom_type: "numeric(12, 2)"
    go_type: "github.com/shopspring/decimal.Decimal"
  }];
}
```

- **`go_type`** is required with `custom_type`, as `"import/path.Type"` or a
  builtin such as `"string"`. It becomes a sqlc type override and the model
  field's type. The type must be one pgx can scan into, which libraries such
  as pgvector-go and shopspring/decimal support ([DAL208](lint-rules.md#dal208)).
- **Extension types** (`vector`, `geometry`, `citext`, …) need their
  extension declared in the file's `(dal.pg.v1.file).extensions`. The schema
  then starts with `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS`.
- **One Go type per SQL type in write parameters.** sqlc types write
  parameters per SQL type, so all columns of one SQL type must share a Go
  type ([DAL213](lint-rules.md#dal213)). For example, if one `numeric` column
  uses `decimal.Decimal`, every `numeric` column must.

## Nullability in Go

The model struct follows the column:

- a required column is a plain value (`string`, `time.Time`);
- a nullable (`optional`) column is a pointer (`*string`, `*time.Time`);
- except for types where nil already means NULL: `[]byte`, slices and
  `json.RawMessage`.

Write parameters are different: every field is a pointer there, so that nil
can mean "use the default" or "missing". See
[Access patterns](queries.md#create).

## Postgres versions and extensions

Two settings describe the Postgres you use:

| Where | What | Example | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `(dal.pg.v1.file)` in the IDL | what the schema **needs** | `{min_version: 16 extensions: ["vector"]}` | 16, no extensions |
| `pg.version` in `dalforge.yaml` | what you **deploy to** | `"16.9"` | `"16"` |

Lint fails if the deploy target is older than a file's `min_version`, or
older than a type or feature in use needs ([DAL207](lint-rules.md#dal207)).
dalforge supports Postgres 16 and later, which is the Aurora PostgreSQL LTS
line it targets.

Every type in the table above exists in Postgres 16. Types added in later
versions will join the `Type` enum with a note on the version they need. The
enum is append-only, so IDL written today keeps working.
